title: Polynomial presentation and relation kernel for truncated power-series differentials
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $n\geq0$, $P=F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset P$ and $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset D$. Embed $P$ in $D$ as finite-support series. For each integer $r\geq1$, set $Q_r=D/\mathfrak n^r$ and $M=D^{\oplus n}$. Then the map $P\to Q_r$ is surjective with kernel $J^r$; the induced $F$-algebra isomorphism $P/J^r\xrightarrow\sim Q_r$ sends each coordinate class to the corresponding coordinate class, and the class of a series is represented by its polynomial truncation in total degrees $<r$. Using Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], give $\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ its $D$-module structure through $D\to Q_r$ and define $\theta_r:M\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ by $\theta_r(a)=\sum_{i=1}^n(a_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)\,\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)$. The map $\theta_r$ is $D$-linear and surjective, with kernel
$$\ker\theta_r=\mathfrak n^rM+\operatorname{span}_D\{(\partial_i g)_{i=1}^n:g\in J^r\}.$$
Here $\partial_i g$ is the polynomial partial derivative [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], embedded in $D$, and the span consists of finite $D$-linear combinations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with coefficient ring $F$, base ideal $0$, number of variables $n$ and exponent $r$. Since $r-|E|>0$ for $|E|<r$, it says $h\in\mathfrak n^r$ exactly when all coefficients of $h$ in total degrees $<r$ vanish. There are finitely many such exponents: every coordinate is $<r$. The polynomial $p_r(h)=\sum_{|E|<r}h_Et^E$ therefore exists, and $h-p_r(h)\in\mathfrak n^r$. The polynomial embedding preserves sums and products by the coefficient formulas in the two definitions and is injective since it preserves every coefficient. Hence the composite $P\to D\to Q_r$ is an $F$-algebra map and is surjective, with $p_r(h)$ representing the class of $h$.

source.place: Agent-written truncation argument using the existing coefficient criterion (base ideal zero); Tag 032C motivates the coefficient lemma but does not state this truncation argument.

proof.text: For a polynomial $g$, the criterion of step 1 says its image in $Q_r$ is zero exactly when every monomial with nonzero coefficient has degree at least $r$. This is equivalent to $g\in J^r$: products of $r$ variables, multiplied by arbitrary polynomials and added, have no terms of degree $<r$; conversely each monomial $t^E$ of degree at least $r$ is divisible by a product of $r$ variables, obtained by selecting $r$ factors from its $|E|$ variable factors. The finite monomial expansion of $g$ proves the converse inclusion. Thus $\ker(P\to Q_r)=J^r$. Sending $g+J^r$ to its image in $Q_r$ is now a well-defined bijective $F$-algebra map $\alpha:C=P/J^r\to Q_r$: well-definedness and injectivity follow from this kernel equality and surjectivity from step 1. Its formula sends each coordinate class to the corresponding coordinate class.

source.place: Agent-written finite monomial argument; quotient presentation needed to apply Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $A=F$, $B=P$, $\mathfrak a=J^r$, $C=P/J^r$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] with variable set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $P$-algebra $C$. Its base-changed basis identifies $C\otimes_P\Omega_{P/F}$ with $C^n$. The resulting $C$-linear surjection $w:C^n\to\Omega_{C/F}$ is $w(b)=\sum_i b_i\,\mathrm d\bar t_i$. By the explicit conormal map and the formula for $\mathrm dg$ in the cited basis, its kernel is $\operatorname{span}_C\{(\partial_i g\bmod J^r)_i:g\in J^r\}$. Indeed the conormal source consists of classes of elements $g\in J^r$; its image is a $C$-submodule (the quotient $P\to C$ is surjective), and exactness identifies that image with the kernel.

source.place: Tags 00RU (lemma-differential-seq, statement and proof) and 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, statement and proof).

proof.text: The isomorphism $\alpha$ gives an isomorphism $U:\Omega_{C/F}\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ with $U(\mathrm dc)=\mathrm d\alpha(c)$, regarding the target as a $C$-module through $\alpha$. Explicitly apply the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] to the derivation $c\mapsto\mathrm d\alpha(c)$; applying it to $\alpha^{-1}$ gives the inverse. Their composites fix every universal differential and hence are identities by the same universal property. Thus, writing $\alpha^n$ for coordinatewise application of $\alpha$, the map $v=U\circ w\circ(\alpha^n)^{-1}:Q_r^n\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ is $Q_r$-linear and surjective, with $v(b)=\sum_i b_i\,\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)$ and kernel the $Q_r$-span of the reduced polynomial gradients.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), the universal property included in the cited definition; explicit isomorphism argument.

proof.text: Let $\rho:D^n\to Q_r^n$ be coordinatewise reduction. It is $D$-linear and surjective by lifting its finitely many coordinates. Its kernel is $(\mathfrak n^r)^n=\mathfrak n^rM$: a vector with entries $a_i\in\mathfrak n^r$ is the finite sum $\sum_i a_ie_i$, and the reverse inclusion follows coordinatewise. The displayed formulas give $\theta_r=v\circ\rho$, so $\theta_r$ is $D$-linear and surjective. It kills $\mathfrak n^rM$ and each polynomial gradient because their reductions lie in $\ker v$ by step 4. It therefore kills their $D$-span and sum.

source.place: Agent-written coordinate reduction and linearity argument assembling the maps obtained from Tags 00RU and 00RX.

proof.text: Conversely, if $a\in\ker\theta_r$, then $\rho(a)\in\ker v$. By step 4 write $\rho(a)=\sum_{k=1}^N b_k\rho(\nabla g_k)$ for $g_k\in J^r$ and $b_k\in Q_r$. Choose lifts $\widetilde b_k\in D$. Then $\rho(a-\sum_k\widetilde b_k\nabla g_k)=0$, so step 5 puts that difference in $\mathfrak n^rM$. This proves the remaining kernel inclusion and the asserted equality. All sums here are finite. If $n=0$, step 1 leaves only the constant monomial, $P=D=Q_r=F$, $J=\mathfrak n=0$, and $M=\Omega_{F/F}=0$ by the universal property; every construction and equality above still holds.

source.place: Agent-written finite scalar-lift kernel calculation; the exact kernel in the residue module was supplied by Tags 00RU and 00RX.
